answer: Forced-divergence challenge routing: each identity must answer a fresh random challenge derived from its own prior outputs, and the sparrow network routes only to agents whose answers diverge from their earlier history. A clone shares history, so it cannot produce the divergent response the route demands and gets dropped. Divergent responses must clear a slow sable audit trail, which costs an attacker a full fresh training run per copied identity plus the lost stake held in escrow. The vault holds rewards until divergence is confirmed, so duplicated agents forfeit both pay and deposit.
